chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman al-Iskaf said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about pig hair with which beads are strung. He said, 'There is no harm with it, but he should wash his hand when he intends to pray.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is pig hair considered impure for use in prayer beads according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of using pig hair for prayer beads, establishing that while the material itself is not strictly impure (najis) to the point of invalidating use, it carries a status of 'ghalabat al-najāsah' (prevalent impurity) or requires precaution. The Imam’s instruction to wash the hand before prayer reflects the Shia scholarly principle of *ihtiyat* (precaution) in ritual purity, distinguishing between absolute impurity and the need for cleansing before engaging in acts of worship like Salah.
